what_its_for: Epoprostenol is used to treat a serious condition called pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which means the blood pressure in the vessels going to your lungs is too high. This medicine helps relax and widen those blood vessels, making it easier for your heart to pump blood and helping you breathe more easily and feel less tired.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a continuous (non-stop) infusion directly into your bloodstream through a small tube called a catheter, which is placed in a large vein near your heart or collarbone. A small pump worn on your body or kept nearby delivers the medicine 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You will receive thorough training from your healthcare team on how to mix, prepare, and use the pump before you go home. Never stop this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping it too quickly can be very dangerous and even life-threatening.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you and will slowly adjust it over time to find the best amount that helps your symptoms without causing too many side effects. The dose is measured in nanograms per kilogram per minute (ng/kg/min). Most patients start at a very low dose and the doctor gradually increases it. Do not change your dose on your own. Always follow your healthcare team's exact instructions for preparing and setting up each dose.
missed_dose: Because this medicine runs continuously through a pump, a 'missed dose' usually means the infusion was interrupted or stopped. Even a short interruption can cause a rapid return of serious symptoms or a dangerous drop in blood pressure. If your pump runs out of medicine, alarms, or stops working, treat it as an emergency. Contact your healthcare team or go to the emergency room right away. Always keep backup supplies of medication and pump batteries on hand.
storage: Storage instructions depend on which brand you use. Flolan must be kept refrigerated (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C) and protected from light. Once mixed and loaded into the pump, it can only be used for a limited time — usually no more than 8 hours at room temperature or 24 hours if kept cold with an ice pack. Veletri can be stored at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) and once mixed, may last up to 48 hours without refrigeration. Always follow your pharmacist's exact instructions for your specific product. Never freeze or shake the medicine. Discard any unused portions as directed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid suddenly stopping this medicine — this can cause a life-threatening emergency. Avoid activities that could accidentally pull out or disconnect your catheter or pump tubing. Avoid infections at the catheter site by always using clean technique when handling supplies. Avoid other blood-thinning medicines, blood pressure-lowering medicines, or supplements (like garlic or fish oil) without checking with your doctor first, as they may increase your risk of bleeding or low blood pressure. Avoid smoking, as it worsens pulmonary hypertension. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine can cause dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if: your pump stops working or alarms; your catheter comes out or looks infected (redness, swelling, pus, fever); you have sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or fainting; you feel very dizzy or lightheaded; you have unusual bleeding or bruising; you notice severe jaw pain, flushing, headache, or muscle/joint pain that becomes unmanageable; you have nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that prevents you from keeping up with your medication routine; or your symptoms of pulmonary hypertension suddenly get worse. Always carry emergency contact numbers with you.
when_it_works: Some patients start to notice improvements in their ability to exercise and breathe within the first few weeks. However, it can take several weeks to months of slow dose adjustments to find your best dose and experience the full benefits. This is a long-term medicine — it helps manage your condition but does not cure it. Keep taking it even when you feel better.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The risks and benefits must be carefully discussed. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects; careful monitoring is needed. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely. Children: This medicine can be used in children with PAH, but dosing and monitoring must be supervised closely by a specialist.
